title: Amazon in Talks with Meta, Considering Opening Up Shopping Through Muse AI Agent

content_html:
Amazon is in talks with Meta to allow its Muse AI agent to shop on Amazon's e-commerce platform. According to Fortune, the discussions focus on the types of products Muse recommends, as well as the potential impact of AI agent shopping on Amazon's ad revenue and customer relationships.

Amazon is concerned that opening access to Muse could weaken its advertising business revenue. Currently, Amazon's advertising system relies on showing ads when real users browse products, while AI agents may change how users discover and choose products. In addition, Amazon is also paying attention to the quality of product search results provided by Muse, and whether the direct relationship between the platform and consumers could be affected after AI agents enter the shopping process.

Currently, retailers such as Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, and Sephora have allowed AI agents like Muse to access their websites, while Amazon has taken a more cautious approach. Previously, Amazon also blocked Perplexity's AI agent from shopping on its platform, instead focusing on promoting its own shopping assistant, Alexa for Shopping. The assistant now supports shopping on behalf of users via text message.

These negotiations reflect the divided attitudes of e-commerce platforms toward AI agent shopping. As AI agents gradually become involved in product search, recommendations, and transactions, how to balance opening up an AI shopping entry point with protecting ad revenue, customer relationships, and platform business interests is becoming a new issue facing the retail industry.
